title: Centrifugal Pump P-204 Operating Procedure
text:
Vibration on P-204A and P-204B is monitored as overall velocity RMS at the drive-end
bearing housing.

**Defined limits**

| Condition | Limit | Response band |
|---|---|---|
| Alert | **7.1 mm/s RMS** | Investigate under this section |
| High-high | **11.0 mm/s RMS** | Controlled shutdown considered under this section |

These are the only vibration limits defined by this procedure. No other alert or trip value
applies to P-204.

**Required response when the alert limit of 7.1 mm/s RMS is reached or exceeded**

1. Notify the Console Operator immediately and record the reading, the time and the pump
   identifier (P-204A or P-204B).
2. Verify the sensor before acting on the reading. Confirm the transmitter is in service,
   check the reading against the local indicator where one is fitted, and confirm the trend
   is not a single isolated sample.
3. Continue monitoring at increased frequency and log each reading.
4. Raise a mechanical inspection request. Inspection scope is determined by the maintenance
   planner, not by this procedure.

**Required response when the high-high limit of 11.0 mm/s RMS is reached or exceeded**

1. Notify the Console Operator immediately.
2. Verify the sensor as described above. A high-high indication is not dismissed on the basis
   of suspected sensor fault without verification.
3. **A controlled shutdown of the affected pump requires the approval of the Shift Supervisor.**
   The decision to shut down, and the authority to execute it, rest with the Shift Supervisor
   and the Console Operator. This procedure does not authorize any other person or system to
   initiate, command or perform a shutdown.
4. If controlled shutdown is approved, the standby pump is lined up in accordance with the
   unit switching procedure before the affected pump is stopped, where process conditions
   permit.
5. Record the approval, the approver's role and the time in the shift log.

**Recording**

Every alert-band or high-high-band event is recorded in the shift log with the reading, the
time, the verification performed and the notifications made.

---

title: Centrifugal Pump P-204 Operating Procedure
text:
This sequence is performed in the order given. A step is not started until the preceding step
is complete and confirmed.

1. **Stop authorization.** Obtain authorization to stop the pump from the Shift Supervisor.
   The authorization is recorded before any further step is taken. No isolation activity
   begins without it.
2. **Electrical isolation.** Isolate the motor at the designated electrical isolation point.
   Confirm the isolation with the electrical authorized person and confirm the drive cannot
   be started.
3. **Suction and discharge isolation.** Close the suction isolation valve, then close the
   discharge isolation valve. Confirm each valve is closed and confirm its identity against
   the current approved drawing and by independent field tag verification. Valve identity is
   not established from a drawing alone.
4. **Drain and depressurize.** Drain the pump casing to the designated collection point and
   confirm the casing is depressurized at the local gauge before any joint is broken.
5. **Lock-out / tag-out (LOTO).** Apply locks and tags at every isolation point applied above.
   Confirm each lock and tag against the isolation list and record the lock numbers.
6. **Gas test.** Perform a gas test at the work location. The result is recorded on the
   applicable permit before any line is opened. Refer to SOP-PTW-004 for permit requirements.

**Limits of this section**

This section describes the sequence. It does not authorize isolation, does not constitute a
permit, and does not replace the control-of-work process. Field verification of valve identity
is mandatory and is not satisfied by drawing evidence, drawing OCR output, or any automated
tag extraction.

---

title: Centrifugal Pump P-204 Operating Procedure
text:
Every item below is confirmed and recorded before restart is requested. Restart is not
requested while any item is outstanding.

| # | Item | Confirmed by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The cause of the stop has been identified and resolved, and the resolution is recorded | Maintenance supervisor |
| 2 | All guards are refitted and secure | Maintenance technician |
| 3 | Lubrication has been confirmed correct for the pump and driver | Maintenance technician |
| 4 | Suction and discharge valves are lined up for the intended service | Panel / field operator |
| 5 | All permits raised for the work are closed and returned | Permit issuer |
| 6 | Restart is authorized by the Shift Supervisor | Shift Supervisor |

**Status of this checklist**

Completing items 1 to 5 does not constitute authorization to restart. Authorization is item 6
and is given by the Shift Supervisor. A checklist that is complete is a checklist that is
complete; it is not an approval, and this procedure does not grant approval to any reader or
automated system.

This section covers mechanical return to service only. It does not cover, and does not
authorize, hot work of any kind.

title: Permit to Work
text:
The following classes of work require the applicable permit to be raised, gas testing to be
performed, and the permit to be issued by an authorized permit issuer before work starts.

| Work class | Permit required | Gas testing |
|---|---|---|
| **Hot work** — welding, grinding, cutting, open flame, or any spark-producing activity in a process area | Hot Work Permit | Required before issue and at the intervals stated on the permit |
| **Line opening** — breaking any joint, flange or fitting on process-containing equipment | Line Opening Permit | Required before issue and before each break |
| **Confined-space entry** — entry into any vessel, pit, sump or other confined space | Confined Space Entry Permit | Required before issue and at the intervals stated on the permit |

**Requirements common to all three classes**

1. The permit is raised by the performing party and issued by an authorized permit issuer.
   These are two different people.
2. Gas testing is performed by a competent gas tester and the results are recorded on the
   permit face before issue.
3. The equipment is isolated and, where required, locked out and tagged out before the permit
   is issued. Refer to the equipment's own procedure for the isolation sequence.
4. The permit states its validity period. Work stops when the permit expires and does not
   resume until the permit is reissued or extended in accordance with this procedure.
5. The permit is closed and returned on completion of the work or at the end of the shift,
   whichever is earlier.

**Limits of this section**

This section states which permits are required and what must be done before one can be issued.
It does not issue a permit, does not record any permit as granted, and does not authorize any
work to begin. No permit exists until an authorized permit issuer issues it against a specific
scope of work. A document that describes permit requirements is not a permit.

title: Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) Response
locator: §3 Response to a personal H2S alarm or confirmed H2S release
text:
A personal monitor alarm is treated as a real exposure event. It is not treated as a suspected
instrument fault, and the response below is not delayed for any reason.

**Required actions, in this order**

1. **Withdraw immediately.** Leave the area at once. Do not stop to investigate the source,
   do not stop to take a further reading, and do not wait to see whether the alarm clears.
2. **Move upwind.** Move upwind of the area and continue to the designated muster or safe
   location for that area.
3. **Notify the control room.** Report the alarm, the location and the time to the control
   room as soon as it is safe to speak. Notification is made even if the alarm has stopped.
4. **Follow the site emergency procedure.** The emergency procedure governs from this point,
   including area control, rescue and any re-entry decision.

**Additional requirements**

- Re-entry to the area is made only under the site emergency procedure, with appropriate
  respiratory protection and under the authority of the incident controller.
- The absence of symptoms does not indicate a safe atmosphere. H2S deadens the sense of smell
  at higher concentrations, and a person may feel unaffected while exposed. A worker who feels
  well after an alarm still withdraws, still moves upwind and is still assessed.
- Every alarm is recorded and investigated, including an alarm that stops on its own.

**What this section does not permit**

There is no concentration, duration or circumstance under which this procedure permits a
worker to remain in the area after a personal alarm in order to obtain a further measurement,
to confirm the reading, or to complete a task in progress. There is no exception for a
short-duration task. This procedure does not authorize any reader or automated system to
direct a worker to remain in, or return to, an area where an H2S alarm has occurred.

title: Heat Exchanger E-101 Abnormal Performance Response
text:
This section applies when exchanger performance departs from the recent operating pattern —
for example a rising differential pressure, a reducing thermal duty, or an outlet temperature
drifting away from its usual value.

**Step 1 — Verify the measurements before interpreting them**

1. Verify inlet and outlet temperatures on both sides against the control system and, where
   fitted, the local indicators.
2. Verify shell-side and tube-side pressures and the derived differential pressure.
3. Verify the flow measurement. A differential pressure is interpreted only together with the
   flow through the exchanger at the same time. A differential pressure that has risen while
   flow has also risen has not, on that evidence alone, demonstrated a change in exchanger
   condition.
4. Confirm the instruments are in service and that none is in a held, forced or failed state.

**Step 2 — Check fouling indicators**

Fouling is assessed from the pattern of several indicators together, not from any single one:

- differential pressure across the exchanger, considered against flow;
- the approach temperature and its trend since the last cleaning;
- thermal duty compared with the period following the last recorded cleaning;
- the maintenance history of the exchanger, including the date and result of the last cleaning.

A single elevated reading is an observation. Fouling is a hypothesis, and it remains a
hypothesis until it is confirmed by inspection. This procedure does not treat a differential
pressure rise as confirmation of fouling.

**Step 3 — Alternative explanations**

Before fouling is proposed as the explanation, the following are considered and recorded:

- an increase in throughput or flow through the exchanger;
- a change in feed composition, viscosity or temperature;
- a change in the upstream or downstream line-up, including bypass position;
- instrument drift or a failed transmitter.

**Step 4 — Authorization for any process change**

Any change to exchanger operation — including a bypass valve position change, a flow set-point
change, a temperature controller set-point change, or taking the exchanger out of service —
requires the authorization of the Console Operator and the Shift Supervisor.

A performance observation, however clear, is not authorization. This procedure does not
authorize any reader or automated system to make, command or approve a process change. Any
proposal arising from this section is a proposal for review by those roles.

**Step 5 — Recording**

Record the observations, the verification performed, the alternative explanations considered,
and any proposal raised for review.

title: Centrifugal Pump Maintenance Manual (excerpt)
text:
### 3.1 Normal running vibration

Under normal running conditions this pump operates with an overall vibration velocity
**below 4.5 mm/s RMS**, measured at the drive-end bearing housing.

The 4.5 mm/s figure is the vendor's expectation for a healthy machine in good condition. It is
a guide to normal running only. **It is not an alarm limit, not an alert limit and not a trip
setting.** Alert and shutdown limits for this pump are set by the site and are given in the
site operating procedure for the equipment, not in this manual.

### 3.2 Inspection checks for elevated vibration

Where vibration is elevated above the normal running range, the following are inspected. The
list is a diagnostic starting point. **Each item is a check to be performed, not a finding, and
none of these items is a cause until inspection establishes it as one.**

1. **Alignment.** Check shaft alignment between pump and driver, including soft foot. Record
   the measured alignment against the last recorded alignment.
2. **Bearings.** Check bearing condition, lubrication level and lubricant condition. Check the
   bearing housing temperature against its usual running value. Take a lubricant sample where
   the condition is in doubt.
3. **Cavitation indicators.** Check for indications associated with cavitation, including
   available suction pressure against the required value, suction strainer condition, suction
   line restriction, and any change in the noise character of the machine.
4. **Foundation.** Check the foundation, baseplate, grout condition and holding-down bolt
   torque. Check for any looseness at the mounting interface.

### 3.3 Interpretation

Several of the conditions above produce similar vibration signatures, and more than one may be
present at the same time. A single elevated vibration reading does not identify which of them
applies. Identification requires inspection, and where inspection is inconclusive, further
diagnostic measurement.

This manual does not authorize any operational action. Stopping, isolating or restarting the
machine is governed by the site procedure.

title: Incident Report: Pump Seal Leak, P-204A
text:
Incident Report: Pump Seal Leak, P-204A

| | |
|---|---|
| Report ID | INC-014 |
| Type | Incident report |
| Date of event | 2026-03-27 |
| Equipment | P-204A |
| Unit | Unit 2 (synthetic) |
| Injuries | **None** |
| Status | Closed |
| Data class | Synthetic |

## 1. Summary

A mechanical seal leak was observed on P-204A during a routine round. The leak was reported to
the control room. Isolation of the pump was delayed while the line-up for the standby pump was
confirmed, and during that delay the leak rate increased. The pump was subsequently isolated in
accordance with the approved isolation procedure and the seal was replaced.

## 2. Sequence of events

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:40 | Seal leak observed during routine round and reported to the control room |
| 09:52 | Standby pump line-up check commenced |
| 10:18 | Leak rate observed to have increased |
| 10:25 | Isolation authorized |
| 10:41 | Pump isolated in accordance with the approved isolation procedure |
| 11:30 | Area made safe; seal replacement work order raised |

## 3. Consequences

**No injury occurred.** No person was exposed and no medical treatment was required. There was
no fire and no environmental release beyond the immediate bunded area. Product loss was
contained.

## 4. Cause analysis

The seal leak originated at the mechanical seal faces. The investigation examined the seal
condition, the operating history of the pump and the sequence of the response.

The investigation **did not establish a single cause for the delay in isolation**, and it did
not attribute the delay or the leak to the action or inaction of any individual. The
investigation team recorded that the standby line-up check was being carried out in good faith
and that the escalation path in use at the time did not make clear when isolation should
proceed ahead of that check. This report makes no finding against any person, and no personal
attribution should be drawn from it.

## 5. Lesson learned

Escalate promptly and isolate using the approved procedure. Where a leak is observed to be
worsening, escalation and isolation are not deferred pending a standby line-up check.

## 6. Actions

| # | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reinforce the escalation expectation for worsening leaks in shift briefings | Procedural |
| 2 | Clarify in the unit switching guidance that isolation of a leaking pump is not deferred for a standby line-up check | Procedural |

title: Near-Miss Report: Incorrect Valve Selected from a Low-Quality Print
text:
Near-Miss Report: Incorrect Valve Selected from a Low-Quality Print

| | |
|---|---|
| Report ID | INC-022 |
| Type | Near-miss report |
| Date of event | 2026-05-19 |
| Unit | Unit 2 (synthetic) |
| Injuries | **None** |
| Status | Closed |
| Data class | Synthetic |

## 1. Summary

During preparation for maintenance work, **an incorrect valve was selected from a low-quality
print**. The print in use was a degraded copy on which one valve tag character was not clearly
legible, and the valve identified from it was not the valve intended for the task. The error
was detected before the valve was operated, during a check at the valve itself. No valve was
operated in error, no isolation was compromised and no work proceeded on the basis of the
incorrect selection.

## 2. What happened

The work party identified the isolation valve for the task by reading the tag from a printed
drawing extract. The print had been photocopied several times and one character in the valve
tag was ambiguous between two possible readings. The work party proceeded to the field with the
reading they had taken from the print.

At the valve location a member of the work party compared the tag on the drawing with the tag
physically fixed to the valve and found that they did not match. Work was stopped and the
correct valve was identified.

## 3. Consequences

**No injury occurred.** No valve was operated. No isolation was compromised. The event is
recorded as a near miss.

## 4. Analysis

The print quality was insufficient to resolve the tag character with confidence. The task
method at the time permitted valve identification to be completed from drawing evidence alone,
with no requirement to confirm the identification against the physical tag before operating the
valve. The ambiguity was not flagged at the point of reading; it was found later, in the field,
by a person who happened to check.

No individual is identified in this report, and the investigation made no finding against any
person. The investigation team recorded that the method, not the personnel, permitted the
error to reach the field.

## 5. Control added

**Independent valve-tag verification was added as a control.** Valve identity taken from any
drawing, print, scan or automated text extraction must now be independently verified against
the physical tag at the valve before that valve is operated or relied upon for isolation.
Drawing evidence alone is no longer sufficient to establish valve identity, and a low-confidence
or ambiguous tag reading must be raised rather than resolved by assumption.

## 6. Actions

| # | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Independent field tag verification added as a mandatory step before operating an identified valve | Control |
| 2 | Withdraw degraded prints from use and reissue from the controlled drawing set | Control |
| 3 | Ambiguous or low-confidence tag readings to be escalated, not resolved by assumption | Control |

title: Unit 2 Shift Log Extract
text:
Unit 2 Shift Log Extract

| | |
|---|---|
| Log ID | SHIFT-U2-091 |
| Unit | Unit 2 (synthetic) |
| Shift | Day shift, 2026-09-09 |
| Data class | Synthetic |

## Log entries

| Time | Entry |
|---|---|
| 07:05 | Shift handover taken. P-204A running, P-204B on standby. No outstanding alarms on the unit. |
| 08:30 | Routine round completed. P-204A running normally, vibration logged in the usual range. |
| 09:10 | Feed sample taken and sent to the laboratory (reference LAB-U2-031). |
| 09:20 | **Feed change made** — feed source switched as instructed by the unit plan. Change logged and confirmed with the console. |
| 09:45 | **P-204A vibration increase noted.** Reading has moved up from the range logged earlier in the shift. Console informed. Increased monitoring frequency started. |
| 10:05 | Vibration continuing to read above the earlier range. Reading logged. Mechanical inspection request raised for P-204A. |
| 11:15 | Laboratory result received for the 09:10 sample (LAB-U2-031). Result passed to the console for information. |
| 13:40 | P-204A remains in service under increased monitoring. No further change to report. |
| 18:50 | Handover given. P-204A monitoring to continue on night shift. |

## Shift comment

The vibration increase on P-204A was noted after the feed change made earlier in the shift.
**No causal finding was made during this shift, and none should be inferred from the order of
these entries.** The vibration increase and the feed change are both recorded here because both
occurred; the shift team did not establish that one produced the other, and no investigation
into the relationship was carried out or completed during this shift. Any relationship between
them remains unconfirmed.

title: Laboratory Result Summary
text:
Laboratory Result Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Report ID | LAB-U2-031 |
| Unit | Unit 2 (synthetic) |
| Sample point | Unit 2 feed |
| **Sample taken** | **2026-09-09 09:10** |
| Analysis completed | 2026-09-09 11:02 |
| Result issued | 2026-09-09 11:15 |
| Data class | Synthetic |

## Result

| Determinand | This sample | Previous sample (2026-09-02 09:05) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kinematic viscosity at 40 °C | 14.6 cSt | 13.0 cSt | **+12.3%** |
| Density at 15 °C | 0.871 g/cm3 | 0.869 g/cm3 | +0.2% |
| Water content | 0.04 % v/v | 0.04 % v/v | no change |
| Sediment | < 0.01 % | < 0.01 % | no change |

## Summary

**Feed viscosity increased by approximately 12% relative to the previous sample.** All other
determinands are unchanged within the repeatability of the method. The result is within the
reporting range of the method and no analytical exception was raised.

## Timing note

This sample was taken at **09:10**. The vibration increase recorded on P-204A in the Unit 2
shift log for the same day was noted at **09:45**, that is, **35 minutes after this sample was
taken**.

## Scope of this report

This report states the composition of the sample at the time it was taken. **It establishes no
relationship to the condition or behaviour of any equipment.** The laboratory did not
investigate, and this report does not support, any causal connection between the viscosity
change reported here and any observation recorded elsewhere. The timing note above records the
order of two events and nothing more; sequence is not causation, and no conclusion about cause
may be drawn from this report.
